subject: Turning an alcove into a workspace
hook: Alcove walls are never straight. This is how a desktop ends up fitting them anyway.
ig:
Alcove walls are never straight. This is how a desktop ends up fitting them anyway.

When you measure an alcove at desk height and again lower down, you'll often get two different widths. Plaster, old brickwork and settling all play a part. A straight-cut desk would leave a tapering gap down one side.

Here's how we deal with it:

- Measure the alcove at more than one height during the survey.
- Cut the desktop in our Hanley workshop and seal the front edge.
- On site, offer it into the alcove and scribe a line that follows the wall.
- Trim to that line so the top sits tight to both sides.
- Fit a cable grommet so leads drop neatly to the socket.

It's the same scribing approach we use on fitted wardrobes and media walls, and it's why built-in furniture looks built in.

Planning a workspace in an alcove? Comment DESK and we'll send you the link.
fb:
Here's a little trade secret: alcove walls are almost never straight.

That's why we measure every alcove at a few different heights, cut the desktop in our Hanley workshop, then scribe it on site so it follows the exact line of the walls. No tapering gaps, no sealant to hide a poor fit. A cable grommet goes in too, so your laptop lead isn't trailing down the wall.
